title: The Detective Boys and the Four Caterpillar Brothers
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Edogawa, Ayumi, Detective Boys, Detective Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old cases/ file's suspect/victim names (Matsuura, Yoshikawa, Shimura) and objects (knife, protective cap) match the transcript, but its clue node c1 ('surviving child witness saw the attacker's face directly') and event e2 location ('Aoyama Cemetery') do not match: the transcript never places the second attack at a cemetery -- it happens in the front yard of Keiichi's own house, among his mother's rose bushes, and Keiichi never actually names or reports the attacker's face to police on-screen (he silently recognizes him and is then ambushed before he can tell anyone). Also, the old file omits the entire cabbage-worm/olive-tree B-plot that supplies the episode's real detective work: Keiichi was secretly relocating caterpillars from his late mother's olive tree to a bigger one at Matsuura Heights each night at 10 PM, which is why he was near the crime scene and why he lied to police about going outside -- not guilt over the murder. The old file also omits Matsuura himself as anything but a suspect name; the transcript uses his claimed chronic 'stiff shoulder' left-arm-clutching as the red herring that superficially matches the taxi driver's description of the culprit, a description that actually fits Yoshikawa bracing stolen cash hidden in his sleeve. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Both Matsuura and the culprit described by the taxi driver clutch their left arm with their right hand -- but Matsuura's is a pre-existing chronic stiff shoulder, while the culprit's only makes sense as someone bracing something hidden in his sleeve after a sudden collision, clearing Matsuura and pointing to Yoshikawa.

Matching scissor-cut branches found on both Keiichi's home olive tree and the Matsuura Heights olive tree reveal Keiichi had been transplanting one cabbage worm per night, explaining his repeated late-night trips without implicating him in the murder.
